skip_reason: Existing-customer service call, not a sales call. Inbound cancellation request on an already-booked Friday move (customer Jana Barker, booked online, moving to a competitor for a 3rd mover at $200/hr). The rep made a retention/save attempt and offered a virtual walkthrough, but never gathered a full inventory, never delivered a quote, and no booking or re-quote occurred. The 9 scorecard sections (agenda, structured probe, pricing walkthrough, clock, estimate, Save Your Ass, booking) do not apply to a cancellation call, so scoring it against the 85 would produce a misleading number.
items_missed: Customer asked twice for a re-quote with three movers ('If you can give me a new quote, I'll consider it') and the rep never produced one — she kept re-offering a virtual walkthrough and an inventory list instead, then closed the call with 'we definitely would need to put eyes on in order to make those changes.' The save was lost on a request the rep could have answered on the spot.

Direct estimate-accuracy complaint went unaddressed: the fiance was quoted ~$750 / 3.5 hours and paid $1,300 for a 6-hour move. The rep explained why the online estimator is imprecise but never acknowledged the miss, never offered to escalate it, and never reset expectations with a corrected range.
Customer twice named stairs as the driver (one set at origin, three-story townhome at destination) and the rep never used that to re-scope crew size or time.
Never quoted the 3-mover option even though she opened with 'we're able to make the same accommodation' — the one competitive lever she had was raised and then dropped.
Did not attempt to hold the Friday slot while the customer decided; the booking was released with no follow-up commitment, no callback time, and no offer to send the new quote by email.

Meet Your Mover was garbled into the objection-handling ('they'll meet the movers feature') rather than pitched as an Einstein differentiator; On-Time Guarantee never mentioned even though the customer's core pain was movers arriving late/slow.
top_strength: She did not just process the cancellation — she pivoted to a save, and led with the right differentiators for this customer: No Worries coverage up to $2,000, no third-party contractors, and no credit card / tax / assembly fees, which directly countered the competitor's $80 credit card fee the customer had just disclosed.
coaching_note: When a customer asks for a number, give the number. Jana asked twice for a quote with three movers and Chauny answered both times with a process ask (virtual walkthrough, full inventory list) instead of a price. She already had the job on file — one bedroom, 1,000 sq ft, stairs at both ends, ~50 boxes, big bedroom set plus a buffet and a workout system — which is more than enough to quote a 3-mover rate and an honest 5-7 hour range on the spot, then offer the walkthrough as the way to tighten it. Quote first, verify second. The related habit: when a customer reports an estimate that missed by 75% ($750 quoted, $1,300 paid), name the miss and own it before explaining the estimator — she explained but never acknowledged, and that is why the price defense never landed.
phone_presence_notes: Warm and non-defensive with real affirmations ('No, absolutely, absolutely. And I do hear everything that you're saying,' 'you're good, you're good') and the customer stayed positive throughout, but the rep used her name only once, filled long stretches with 'mm-hmm' and 'uh-huh' instead of steering, and her explanations ran on until the customer had to cut the call short to get to work.
